title: Practical operational guide for marketplaces
subtitle: What a small or medium-sized platform selling goods in Poland and the EU should build and do
description: Decision rules, scope of responsibility, product requirements, and implementation order for marketplaces - from business model to GO / NO-GO checklist.

chapters.title: 0. How to use the guide

segments.text: This guide describes what a small or medium-sized marketplace owner needs to decide, build, show to users, and archive. It is not a code specification. It assumes the sale of physical goods to consumers in Poland, with the possibility of allowing sellers from other EU or non-EU countries.

The document covers common requirements for a typical marketplace: consumer law, pricing and reviews, GPSR and product safety, DSA, P2B, GDPR/RODO, cookies and marketing, DAC7, BDO and packaging, payments, VAT, accessibility, and cybersecurity. Regulated goods - for example, food, cosmetics, toys, electronics, medical devices, alcohol, or chemicals - require an additional industry-specific gateway described in Chapter 7.

blocks.label: IMPORTANT
blocks.text: The material presents an author's interpretation of sources verified as of August 30, 2026. It is for informational and educational purposes only. It does not constitute legal, tax, accounting, or technical advice, nor a recommendation for a specific case. It should not be the sole basis for business decisions or product compliance assessment.
One pattern for each obligation

segments.text: Each chapter should be read in the same order:
Who it concerns - whether the obligation applies to the operator now, only after crossing a threshold, or primarily to the seller.
What result is required - e.g., the ability to accept a report, restore a version, block an offer, or find buyers.
The simplest MVP - using an existing form, order record, offer status, change history, file, or controlled spreadsheet, if it provides the required result.
What proof to keep - content, time, source, decision, and action taken within the appropriate scope for the matter.
When to expand - a dedicated panel, separate table, automation, integration, and dashboard appear only when scale, response time, permissions, or a specific regulation requires it.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: If the information is already in the database, has a permanent identifier and timestamp, can be searched, linked to a user/offer/order, and restored after data changes, then usually there is no need to create a second register solely for compliance. The exception is when the existing record can be overwritten, lacks required elements, does not have proper retention, or access to it does not allow fulfilling the obligation within the deadline.
A principle that removes 'room for interpretation' from platform operations

segments.text: The law often depends on facts. Therefore, the platform should not guess. It should use three states:
APPROVED - required information and evidence are complete, and the product falls within the approved category.
TO BE COMPLETED - sales are blocked until the seller provides the missing evidence or corrects the offer.
REQUIRES SPECIALIST DECISION - sales remain blocked, and a lawyer, tax advisor, or product specialist resolves the specific case. The decision is recorded and applied to all identical cases.

blocks.label: STOP
blocks.text: If the system cannot unambiguously determine the seller, manufacturer, importer, responsible EU person, entity responsible for packaging, or the obligations for a given category - do not publish the offer and do not accept payments.

blocks.text: Glossary of simple roles

segments.text: Operator - the company running the marketplace service.
Seller - the entity with whom the buyer enters into a sales agreement. It can be a business or a private individual, if the platform allows it.
Manufacturer - an entity that produces a product or commissions its design/production and offers it under its own name or brand. A craftsperson making a mug is a manufacturer.
Importer - an entity based in the EU that first places a product from a third country on the EU market.
Distributor - an entity making a product available in the supply chain, but not being the manufacturer or importer.
Responsible person in the EU - for some products, an entity based in the EU whose details must accompany the offer and product when the manufacturer is outside the EU.

Packaged product placer - an entity that, in situations defined by law, is the first to make a packaged product available in Poland, imports it, or packages a product before placing it on the market. This is a BDO role, not a synonym for seller.

chapters.title: 1. First choose the business and responsibility model, then build the marketplace

segments.text: The biggest mistake of a small marketplace is starting with a catalog, cart, and payments without determining who actually sells, accepts money, packs, imports, and handles complaints. These decisions change almost every subsequent obligation.

blocks.text: Base model recommended for small and medium-sized operators

segments.text: In a safe starting model:
each product has a clearly indicated seller;
the buyer enters into a sales agreement directly with the seller;
the operator provides an intermediation service and does not take title to the goods;
a licensed payment provider distributes funds and conducts the KYC required for payments;
the seller is responsible for product compliance, shipping, withdrawal, complaint, and sales documentation;
the operator is responsible for the interface, information, verification required by regulations, evidence, moderation, and case referral;
the operator does not import, repackage, or apply its own brand until a separate compliance process is launched.

blocks.label: DECISION
blocks.text: This model limits risk but does not exempt the operator from GPSR, DSA, consumer law, GDPR/RODO, DAC7, P2B, or obligations regarding prices, reviews, and availability.

blocks.text: Decisions that must exist in a single “model document”

segments.text: Before inviting the first seller, the management approves a short document describing:
Who is a party to the sales agreement and where the buyer sees this information.
Who issues the receipt or invoice.
Who sets the price, promotion, delivery cost, and deadline.
Who accepts withdrawal, complaints, and refund requests.
Who packs and ships, and who accounts for packaging.
Who imports, if the product comes from outside the EU.
Who stores product documentation and handles recalls.
How the PSP accepts funds, verifies the seller, makes distributions, and handles chargebacks.
Who is the data controller in each process.
Which categories, seller countries, and delivery destinations are allowed at the start.

blocks.label: EVIDENCE
blocks.text: Keep the approved version of the model document, the agreement with the PSP, sample agreements with the customer and seller, and the responsibility map. Changes to fulfillment, import, own brand, or money flow require a new review before implementation.

chapters.title: 2. Construction plan: what must exist and when

blocks.text: Stage A - before signing an agreement with the first seller

segments.text: Approved responsibility model and list of allowed categories.
Agreement and terms and conditions for sellers, covering P2B, division of responsibilities, product documents, BDO, DAC7, payouts, complaints, recalls, and penalties.

Seller verification process and the ability to retain documents and decision history. In MVP, this can be fields/statuses of an existing seller account and files in a controlled storage – a separate module is not required.
Agreement with a payment provider supporting marketplaces.
DSA procedure: content/product notifications, moderation, justification of decisions, and appeals to the extent required.
GPSR procedure: blocking, notification, recall, buyer notification, and contact with the authority.
Privacy policy, GDPR role map, data processing agreements, and record of processing activities.
DAC7 decision: whether the operator is a reporting operator and what data it will collect.

blocks.text: Stage B - before publishing the first offer

segments.text: Product card enforcing seller, manufacturer, responsible person in the EU, product identification, warnings, and category information.
Category approval process and blocking publication if information is missing.
Ability to attach compliance documents and proof of origin to the seller or offer. In MVP, existing file storage with access control and record association is sufficient.
Visible indication of whether the seller is a business or a private individual.
Rules for ranking, advertisements, reviews, and promotions.
Price change history and calculation of the lowest price over 30 days. In MVP, this can be a record of each change and a query performed during promotions; a separate pricing engine is not necessary.

blocks.text: Stage C - before accepting the first paid order

segments.text: Checkout indicating the seller for each item, total price, fees, delivery, and payment obligation.

Checkbox for accepting terms and conditions with proof allowing reconstruction of the person, time, and applicable version – not as marketing consent. The law does not mandate a separate technical table.
Separate, voluntary marketing consents and a cookie panel blocking optional technologies until consent is given.
Order snapshot: seller, product, price, offer, warnings, document versions, and proof of acceptance.
Path for withdrawal, complaint, return, refund, and communication with the seller.
Payment processing, payouts, holds, refunds, and chargebacks by the PSP.
Account security: MFA for administrators and high-risk local operations, roles, logs, and backups. Payout operations performed solely within Stripe are secured by Stripe.

blocks.text: Stage D - before public scaling

segments.text: Availability report and the entire purchasing process available.
Established schedule for audits of offers, sellers, BDO, DAC7, security, and retention.

Event view: blocked products, missing documents, notifications, deadlines, complaints, recalls, and incidents. Initially, this can be a saved query or a controlled export/spreadsheet; a dedicated dashboard is only needed for a larger volume of cases.
Business continuity plan, backup recovery, and data breach handling.
Assessment of DSA, PAD, and NIS2 thresholds with an alert before losing exemption or reaching a threshold.

chapters.title: 4. Seller Onboarding: Whom to Allow to Sell

segments.text: Onboarding cannot be a single survey of 'company/private person'. It must establish roles, upon which consumer law, product safety, BDO, VAT, DAC7, and payouts depend.

blocks.text: Onboarding Scope - Do Not Duplicate Payment Provider Data

segments.text: The platform collects data directly only if it needs it for its own service and obligations. For a typical marketplace, these are:
full name or company name, entrepreneur/private person/unregistered business status, address, and contact details;
country of registered office and shipping countries;
NIP/TIN, EU VAT number, KRS or relevant registry and number - if applicable;
product roles: manufacturer, importer, distributor, brand owner, dropshipper;
information on who warehouses, packs, and dispatches the shipment;
categories and brands the seller wishes to offer;
BDO/EPR and scope of registration, where applicable, or specific basis for exemption;
identification data required for DAC7, if the operator is subject to reporting;
acceptance of product compliance, recalls, complaints, and sanctions policies.

A payout account does not need to be copied to the marketplace database simply because Stripe or another PSP has it. In the Stripe Connect model, the platform may only store the account identifier with the PSP, verification and payout status, country/currency, and events necessary for transaction reconciliation. The full account number and KYC documents can remain solely with the PSP if the platform does not need them for its own obligations.
There are two exceptions:

DAC7: the financial account identifier is reported only if it is available to the operator. It is not necessary to obtain the full account solely to make it 'available'. If Stripe provides the operator with the required identifier or reference data, it should be included in the report.

Article 30 DSA: the obligation to obtain and securely store payment account data applies to marketplaces to which Section 4 of the DSA applies; micro and small operators are generally exempt from it. Upon losing exemption, the PSP may be a source of data, but the agreement and integration must ensure the operator fulfills the DSA obligation. The mere fact that Stripe has data to which the operator has no legal or technical access is not sufficient for a medium-sized operator covered by Article 30.

blocks.label: DECISION
blocks.text: For Artovni: do not add an IBAN field or a copy of KYC documents in the seller panel if Stripe Connect handles onboarding and payouts. Record the Stripe account ID, onboarding completion status, payment/payout enablement status, and history of significant changes. Expand the scope only after entering Article 30 of the DSA or when a specific report requires data actually available to the operator.

compliance documents and marking appropriate for the category;

chapters.title: 5. Product card: information without which an offer cannot be published

segments.text: The product card is not solely marketing material. It is the place for fulfilling pre-contractual obligations, GPSR, DSA, and industry-specific regulations. The absence of a mandatory element must result in blocking publication, not a yellow warning that the seller can ignore.

blocks.text: Common minimum - this is not an 'Amazon' form

segments.text: For GPSR, a common form can be brief. A business entity's offer should include:
a photo and the name/type of product and an identifier allowing to determine which product the offer concerns;
the manufacturer's name and its postal and electronic address;
if the manufacturer is outside the EU - the name and postal and electronic address of the responsible person in the EU;
warnings and safety information in Polish only if the product requires them;
the seller, the full price, delivery, and other consumer information relevant to this offer.

There is no general obligation to enter the weight, all dimensions, composition, capacity, serial number, and dozens of parameters for every product. Such fields are activated only for categories where such information is legally required or necessary for safe use and a fair description.

blocks.label: DECISION
blocks.text: Build a two-layer form: 5–7 common blocks for all listings and short category modules, e.g., composition for cosmetics, allergens for food, CE for toys, material and intended use for food-contact ceramics. The seller does not see fields from other categories.
Is a photo of the label sufficient?

segments.text: The law requires information to be clearly and visibly available in the offer; it does not mandate a specific database structure. A legible photo of the label can provide some information and is good evidence, but it should not be the sole mechanism for key data.
Minimum variant for the platform:
the seller adds a clear photo of the entire label/packaging, with the possibility of zooming;
in short fields or an automatically extracted summary, the platform displays the manufacturer, the responsible person in the EU, the product identifier, and the most important warnings;
the remaining composition, instructions, and markings can remain on a legible photo or in an attached document, if category regulations do not require a better presentation method;
a human or automated check rejects blurry, cropped photos, photos in a foreign language without Polish information, or photos depicting a different version of the product.

The photo alone is insufficient if the text is illegible on a phone, the manufacturer remains unsearchable, warnings are not accessible to a screen reader user, or the label does not contain all required information.

blocks.text: Handicrafts and unique items

segments.text: A craftsperson is a manufacturer but does not have to invent a model and series that do not actually exist. For a unique painting, mug, or piece of jewelry, the identifier can be the title/name, author's designation, year or date of creation, and a unique item number or another element assigned to the item. The identifier should be on the product, packaging, or a tag attached to the product, and in the offer – not exclusively in the marketplace's internal number.

Instructions and warnings are not mandatory 'for the sake of it'. If a product can be safely used as intended without instructions and warnings, GPSR does not require the creation of fictitious text. A safety analysis appropriate to the product remains required.

segments.text: If multiple sellers use a single shared product card, each of them must still be correctly assigned to their offer. A shared description cannot overwrite other variants, manufacturers, importers, or warnings. chapters.title: 6. GPSR: Product Safety in Practice

segments.text: The General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR) applies from 13 December 2024 to consumer products offered in the course of a commercial activity, unless sector-specific rules govern the relevant risk. A trader or other entity acting in a commercial capacity is not exempt merely because the product is handmade, turnover is low, or the model is dropshipping. A small manufacturer may keep simpler documentation proportionate to the risk, but the product must still be safe and identifiable. Purely occasional consumer-to-consumer sales are a separate case described above.

blocks.text: What the operator must ensure - and how to do it in an MVP

segments.text: The law describes functions, not the number of forms, tables, or panels. For a small marketplace, the minimum implementation looks like this:

Contact point for authorities. A separate 'for authorities' application is not required. A publicly indicated email address or a form allowing direct communication, not requiring an account, is sufficient. The simplest approach is to create an alias like legal@... or safety@..., which forwards to an existing inbox/ticketing system, and a category 'Public Authority - Product Safety'. This contact point's details must be provided during platform registration on the Safety Gate portal and kept up-to-date.

Contact point for consumers. This can be the current Artovni support form. A second page does not need to be built. In the 'Report Type' field, a visible option 'Product Safety / Dangerous Product' should be added, and next to the form, an email address or another communication channel allowing contact with a human should be provided. Communication cannot rely solely on a bot.

Separation of paths, not systems. Authorities and consumers can be directed to the same table and the same team. Category, priority, and deadline allow for service separation. 'Separate point' means a recognizable destination and appropriate message routing, not necessarily separate code or database.

Safety Gate registration and message reception. Initially, a designated person checking the inbox and portal daily on business days, and a deputy for absences, is sufficient. API integration and automatic offer matching are solutions for larger scale operations, not a starting requirement.

Information in the offer. The product form should accept and display only the GPSR-required data for the specific product: manufacturer, EU responsible person, identification, and existing safety warnings/information. A universal form with hundreds of fields should not be created.

Case reception. The current form is sufficient after adding a case type and the ability to provide a link or offer/product identifier, risk description, contact details, and an attachment. If the data can be entered in the description field, separate fields do not need to be created immediately; it is important that the team can identify the product and assess the risk.

Case recording. A dedicated 'safety panel' is not required. An existing case record can serve as a GPSR case if it retains the content, attachments, product/offer, seller, time of receipt, status, deadline, decision, communication, and actions taken. Access must be restricted to authorized personnel.

Case identifier. A UUID assigned to each request is a sufficient operational identifier. GPSR does not mandate a case number format. It is advisable to display this UUID or a shorter number in the email confirmation so that the reporter and support staff refer to the same case.

Blocking and searching for similar offers. In an MVP, changing the offer status to blocked and manually searching for other offers by manufacturer, name, photo, code, or seller is sufficient. Automatic similarity detection is only needed when manual checks prevent meeting deadlines or an order requires proportional searching of identical content.

Identifying buyers. A second 'buyer list' does not need to be stored. It is sufficient if, from order positions, one can search for individuals who purchased a specific offer/product/batch, export the results, and send notifications. If batches are not used, searching is done by product or offer identifier.

Cooperation and withdrawal. A brief instruction is needed: who blocks the offer, who responds to the authority, who determines the scope of buyers, who sends the notification, and who closes the case. This can be a one-page procedure and message templates, not a separate workflow module.

The rest of the current form - name/company, email, subject, description, and attachments - can remain common.

blocks.label: DECISION
blocks.text: Expand this into a dedicated panel only when the number of cases leads to missed deadlines, multiple teams work on a single withdrawal simultaneously, batches and offers need to be merged en masse, or manual buyer searches become unreliable.

blocks.text: How a case should proceed

segments.text: Accept the signal. The existing request UUID is its identifier; do not create a second number if the current one is persistent and searchable.
Temporarily block the offer if the risk may affect health or safety.
Identify identical products, variants, batches, other sellers, and all orders.
Secure offer content, evidence, correspondence, and product data.
Request documents and responses from the seller/manufacturer within a short deadline that does not violate the operator's deadline.
Check Safety Gate and communications from relevant authorities.
Make a documented decision: reinstatement, correction, permanent blocking, warning, or withdrawal.
Notify the authority and consumers when required; monitor the implementation of the corrective measure.
Block re-listing and use the case to audit similar products.

blocks.label: STOP
blocks.text: Contractual clauses stating 'the seller is responsible for the product' do not allow the operator to leave an offer online when the operator knows or should know about a risk.
Artisan and ceramic mug

segments.text: An artisan who makes a mug and sells it under their own name or brand is considered the manufacturer. They must, among other things:
design and manufacture a product that is safe under normal and foreseeable use;
conduct and retain a risk assessment and adequate technical documentation;
enable identification of the product/batch and manufacturer;
provide warnings and instructions if necessary;
respond to complaints, incidents, and dangerous products;
for food contact cups, also comply with food contact material regulations, including substance migration.

The platform does not require documentation created for a factory from a craftsperson, but requires real proof corresponding to the product and risk. The declaration "handmade" itself is not proof of safety.

blocks.text: Dropshipping

segments.text: Dropshipping is a logistics method, not a legal exemption. The platform determines:
who the seller is towards the customer;
where the goods are located at the time of sale;
who is the first to bring them into the EU;
who is the importer and the responsible person in the EU;
who has the product documents and batch numbers;
who will carry out the withdrawal and accept the return;
who will account for packaging, VAT, and customs duties.

blocks.label: STOP
blocks.text: Direct shipment from a third country without an established importer/responsible person, documents, and a real return means the seller or product is not permitted.

chapters.title: 8. BDO, packaging, and EPR: who is actually responsible

segments.text: BDO does not automatically apply to everyone who sells. It applies to specific roles and product groups. In a marketplace, the most common obligation arises when an entity packages a product and is the first to introduce it in that packaging in Poland, imports/acquires the product in packaging from another EU country or from outside the EU, offers its own brand, or introduces equipment, batteries, tires, oils, or products covered by other BDO sections.
Do not confuse the two questions:
GPSR: who is the manufacturer/importer/distributor and is the product safe?
BDO/EPR: who introduces packaging or a specific product group to the market and has an obligation to register/account for it?
The same person may have both roles, one of them, or neither.

blocks.text: Platform rule for packaging

segments.text: First, determine the seller's status. The Polish BDO obligation for "introducers of products in packaging" applies to an entrepreneur conducting business activity. BDO should not be automatically requested from a person who occasionally sells privately, nor - as a rule - from a person properly conducting unregistered business activity, which according to the Entrepreneurship Law is not business activity.
Only from a seller who is an entrepreneur does the platform determine:
Are they importing a product in packaging from another EU country or from outside the EU?
Are they packaging their own or someone else's product themselves and are the first to introduce it in that packaging in Poland?
Are you adding unit, collective, or shipping packaging before sending to the customer?
Does the product belong to a group covered by a separate BDO/EPR entry, e.g., electrical equipment, batteries, tires, oils, or single-use products?

If the entrepreneur answers 'yes', the platform requires the identification of the responsible entity, the BDO number, and the relevant scope of the entry, or documented proof why the obligation rests with another entity.

blocks.label: IMPORTANT
blocks.text: 'I do it out of passion' is not a legal category. A person can be a private seller, run an unregistered business, or be an entrepreneur. The platform asks about status and sales method, not emotional motivation.

blocks.label: STOP
blocks.text: The checkbox 'BDO does not apply to me' without a supply chain description is insufficient. Sales can only be activated once it is known who is packaging, who is importing, and who is the first to introduce this packaging or product into Poland.

blocks.text: The 1 Mg threshold - what it really means

segments.text: An entrepreneur introducing no more than 1 Mg of packaging per year may, after meeting de minimis aid conditions and submitting documents on time, obtain an exemption from certain financial obligations, including the product fee and specific duties. This does not automatically mean no BDO registration, record-keeping, or annual reporting.

For micro-entrepreneurs, the registration fee is currently PLN 200, and the annual fee is also PLN 200 until the end of February. In the year of paying the registration fee, the annual fee is not paid additionally. For other entities, the rate is PLN 800.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: A candle illustrates why the question must concern packaging. Shipping cartons and sales boxes are typical packaging. The glass container itself, in which the candle burns throughout its use, may require separate qualification as a product component and should not be automatically counted like a carton.

blocks.label: DEADLINE
blocks.text: For a typical introducer of products in packaging: registration before commencing the obligated activity; annual fee by the end of February; reporting and the relevant de minimis application generally by March 15 for the previous year. Deadlines and scope must be confirmed for the specific BDO department.
PPWR from August 12, 2026 - a new EU layer

segments.text: Regulation (EU) 2025/40 on packaging and packaging waste (PPWR) is being applied in stages from August 12, 2026. It does not immediately replace all national BDO/EPR mechanisms; it adds common requirements for packaging in the EU.
As of today, the platform should implement the following rules:
packaging placed on the EU market must meet the applicable PPWR requirements, including the general requirement for recyclability; detailed recycling design classes will be phased in later;
food-contact packaging must not exceed the PFAS limits applicable from August 12, 2026; for flower shops, this applies to food additives, for example, not the bouquet itself;
the entity designing/manufacturing the packaging and the entity introducing it must store the required documentation and perform their roles in accordance with PPWR;
for new packaging materials, the fulfillment provider/operator collects the supplier's specification and proof of conformity, not just the purchase invoice;

the development plan includes later deadlines: harmonized labels around 2028, and from 2030, among others, a limit of maximum 50% empty space for e-commerce and transport packaging, according to a future calculation method.

An average marketplace, to which Section 4 of Chapter III of the DSA applies, before allowing a producer offering packaging or a product in packaging to consumers in the EU, obtains for the consumer's country:
information about the producer's registration in the relevant EPR register and the registration number; and
self-certification that it only offers packaging that meets the obligations of extended producer responsibility.

Subsequently, it makes best efforts to assess the completeness and reliability of the information, particularly through official registers. A micro/small operator exempted from the relevant DSA section still complies with Polish BDO and other regulations, and it is worth building the same mechanism earlier, as it will be needed after growth and when selling to other countries.

blocks.label: STOP
blocks.text: After the PPWR enters into force, the BDO number for Poland is not a universal "packaging passport" for the entire EU. Sales to a consumer in another country require establishing EPR registration and a representative in that country in accordance with the PPWR.

from an entrepreneur subject to the obligation – the BDO number and the entity name consistent with the register;
the scope/field of entry corresponding to the role and products, not just the number;
indication of who is packaging and who holds data on packaging weight;
confirmation of update upon change of fulfillment, import, or category;
for a seller without a number: a specific description of the chain and the responsible entity, approved in the exception process;
annual reminder before the end of February and March 15;
blocking a new category if it requires a different BDO field.

blocks.text: The operator does not settle BDO for sellers, but cannot ignore deficiencies

segments.text: In the standard model, the seller-entrepreneur subject to the obligation performs their own registration, record-keeping, payments, and reporting. The operator:
describes the requirement in the agreement;
collects and periodically checks the number and role only from entities to whom the obligation applies;
enables data export on sales if it can help the seller with record-keeping;
transmits reports from fulfillment on material weights attributed to the seller, if such a model is agreed upon;
suspends the category or sale if the required obligation is not clarified.

blocks.label: IMPORTANT
blocks.text: BDO is a multi-area register. A number obtained for waste or one type of product does not prove fulfillment of obligations for packaging, batteries, or electrical equipment.

chapters.title: 9. Consumer Law: Sale, Withdrawal, and Complaint

blocks.text: Before concluding the contract

segments.text: The buyer should receive clearly and without having to search through multiple documents:
seller's identity and contact details;
information on whether the seller is an entrepreneur;
main product features and offer content;
total price including taxes and all additional fees;
delivery cost and method, execution deadline, and limitations;
payment, withdrawal, return, and complaint procedures;
duration of commitments, if they do not end with a one-time purchase;
information on functionality/compatibility for digital content or services, if applicable;
division of responsibilities between the platform and the seller.

blocks.text: Checkout without pitfalls

segments.text: The summary groups items by seller.
Each item shows price, quantity, delivery, and fees.
The total amount matches the amount charged by PSP.
The button to place an order clearly states "order with payment obligation" or an equivalent clear statement.
Paid add-ons are not pre-selected.
Links to terms and conditions and withdrawal policy are available before clicking, and a copy or confirmation is sent to the customer on a durable medium.
The platform saves the version of the terms and conditions and the summary shown at the time of purchase.

blocks.label: STOP
blocks.text: The text on buttons like "next," "confirm," or "register" is insufficient if clicking it creates a payment obligation.
Withdrawal from the contract

segments.text: Typically, a consumer has 14 days to withdraw from a contract concluded online. For goods, the period starts from receipt; for multiple items delivered separately, it follows the rule for the last delivery. Lack of proper information may extend the withdrawal period by up to 12 months.

The platform should provide a simple form with options to select the order and product, and upon submission, immediately confirm the request on a durable medium. The matter is then forwarded to the relevant seller, but the operator monitors deadlines and status. In an MVP, this could be the same support form and the same request record with the type "withdrawal."

The seller refunds payments, including the cost of the cheapest standard delivery offered, generally within 14 days of receiving the declaration. They may withhold the refund until they receive the goods or proof of return, whichever comes first. Exceptions to withdrawal, e.g., for custom-made products, can only be applied if they genuinely meet the criteria and the buyer was informed before purchase.

blocks.text: Complaint of conformity of goods with the contract

segments.text: In consumer sales, the entrepreneur is liable for any lack of conformity of the goods that becomes apparent within 2 years of delivery. The consumer may first request repair or replacement, and in statutory cases, a price reduction or withdrawal. The seller should respond to the complaint within 14 days; failure to respond implies acceptance of the complaint.
The marketplace ensures:
submission with request category, description, evidence, and order item;
automatic confirmation of submission date;
submission date, 14-day deadline, and escalation before expiry – even in a daily queue or calendar;
communication within a single thread, accessible to the customer, seller, and authorized support staff;
seller's decision with justification and method of execution;
handling of shipment, exchange, repair, return, and refund;
statistics on recurring defects as a GPSR signal.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: A separate complaints module is not required at the start. An existing form/ticket is sufficient if it is linked to the order and seller, saves the request and attachments, sends a confirmation, and allows setting a 14-day deadline. Initial deadlines can be monitored by an employee in their daily view or calendar. Automatic escalations become necessary when manual control is no longer reliable.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: A complaint about product quality can be a safety signal. Phrases like 'electrocution,' 'fire,' 'cut,' 'poisoning,' 'child swallowed,' 'battery exploded,' or a series of similar defects trigger a parallel GPSR assessment, not just a standard return.

chapters.title: 10. Prices, Promotions, Ranking, Advertising, and Reviews

blocks.text: Lowest Price from 30 Days

segments.text: When a seller communicates a price reduction - a crossed-out price, a percentage, the phrase "promotion," "cheaper," or an equivalent message - the lowest price applied in the 30 days prior to the reduction is displayed next to the current price. If the product has been offered for less than 30 days, the lowest price since the start of the offer is displayed. A special rule applies to perishable goods.
The platform must:
store the price history for each offer and variant;
calculate the period based on the price actually offered to consumers, not the supplier's catalog price;
display the information in the same location and for the same variant as the promotion;
update it consistently on the list, product page, in the cart, at checkout, and in internal advertising;
block manual entry of a more favorable "30-day price" by the seller;
retain proof of calculation.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: There is no need to build a separate "Omnibus module." If every price change has a timestamp and value, the lowest price can be calculated from the existing offer history when a promotion is activated. A separate table is only needed if the current record stores only the current price and overwrites the previous one.

blocks.label: STOP
blocks.text: Increasing the price for a few days does not create a legal "regular price." The lowest price from the last 30 days is the reference point, even if marketing wants to show a larger discount.
Ranking and Paid Visibility

segments.text: In search results or in an easily accessible explanation, the platform provides the main parameters determining the order and their relative importance. It does not disclose the algorithm or security measures but explains the actual factors, e.g., relevance, price, availability, delivery time, service quality, popularity, and paid promotion.

Any paid increase in visibility is clearly marked as advertising/sponsored offer. If the operator sells their own goods or favors a partner, they describe this in the seller terms and conditions and in the ranking information.

blocks.text: Reviews

segments.text: The platform publishes information on whether and how it verifies that a review comes from a person who purchased or used the product. It then acts precisely according to this declaration.
The "verified purchase" label is awarded exclusively to reviews linked to a genuinely completed order.
Unverified reviews may be allowed but are marked differently.
Purchased, generated, duplicated, or manipulated reviews are prohibited, as is the selective publication of only positive ones without disclosing the rules.
Moderation of offensive content or personal data must not remove fair criticism simply because it is negative.
A seller cannot make benefits conditional on leaving a positive review.
The platform stores the reason for moderation and allows for appeals to the required extent.

blocks.text: Personalized Pricing

segments.text: If the price has been individually adjusted based on automated decision-making, the consumer receives clear information before purchase. General segmentation and coupons with fixed rules are not always personalized pricing; however, the platform must describe the mechanism and obtain a GDPR assessment if it uses profiling.

chapters.title: 11. Payments, Payouts, VAT, and Sales Documents

blocks.text: Secure Money Flow

segments.text: A small and medium marketplace should use a licensed payment provider offering a marketplace product: seller onboarding, accounts/sub-accounts, payment splitting, payout schedules, refunds, chargebacks, holds, and reconciliation reports.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: In the Stripe Connect model, the platform saves the Stripe account ID, payment/refund statuses, and IDs needed for order association. The Artovni panel can remain solely a view of history and statistics. It is not necessary to replicate account changes, payouts, KYC, or security measures performed on Stripe's hosted screens within it.

blocks.label: STOP
blocks.text: Do not accept the full price into the operator's regular account only to transfer part of it to the seller after a few days, unless a payment lawyer has confirmed the basis in writing. The mere statement "the operator acts as an agent" does not create an exemption from payment regulations.

segments.text: The agreement and platform functions define:
who is the acquirer and recipient of funds;
when the consumer's payment is considered made to the seller;
conditions for payout and its suspension;
the method for full and partial refunds with multiple sellers;
responsibility for chargebacks, fraud, and negative balances;
PSP fees and operator commission;
reconciliation of orders-payments-refunds-payouts;
procedures following seller suspension or product withdrawal.

blocks.text: Invoice, Receipt, and Platform Confirmation

segments.text: If the seller is the party to the sale, they are responsible for the correct sales document and tax on their supply. The operator documents their own commission/service. The platform's "order confirmation" email should not resemble the seller's invoice if it is not one.
The buyer receives a breakdown by seller. The system allows each seller to download data necessary for their settlements but does not share data of other sellers.

blocks.text: When a Marketplace May Be Considered a Supplier for VAT

segments.text: In specific transactions, an electronic platform may be treated as an entity for VAT purposes that has itself acquired and supplied the goods, including when it facilitates:
distance selling of imported consignments with a real value not exceeding EUR 150; or
delivery of goods in the EU to a consumer when the relevant seller is not based in the EU.

Then VAT collection, invoicing, record-keeping, OSS/IOSS, and liability change. Additionally, an interface facilitating specific transactions may be obliged to store detailed records for 10 years, even when it is not the deemed supplier.

blocks.label: DECISION
blocks.text: If you allow a seller from outside the EU or direct shipping from a third country, launch a separate tax and customs project before the first offer. Do not resolve this solely by setting the VAT rate in the catalog.
Cross-border sales in the EU

segments.text: OSS can simplify the settlement of specific B2C sales in the EU, and IOSS for specific shipments imported up to EUR 150. Who uses the procedure depends on the role of the supplier and the platform. The system must store the consumer's country, the basis for determining the place of supply, amounts, rates, returns, and adjustments in a manner agreed upon with a tax advisor.

chapters.title: 12. GDPR without myths: what to record, where, and on what basis

blocks.text: Acceptance of terms and conditions: proof required, separate table not required

segments.text: Acceptance of the terms and conditions is not GDPR consent for order fulfillment. Data necessary for the account, order, payment, security, and legal obligations are processed on the appropriate basis, e.g., contract performance, legal obligation, or legitimate interest. Do not force 'GDPR consent' which, if withdrawn, would prevent the fulfillment of the concluded contract.

The 'I accept the terms and conditions' checkbox is a contractual declaration. The law primarily requires that the terms and conditions be made available before the contract is concluded in a manner that allows them to be obtained, reproduced, and stored, and that the operator can demonstrate which content was in effect. No provision mandates the creation of a table with a specific name or a separate acceptance table for this reason.
However, the operator must have reliable proof that allows linking:
who accepted;
the date and exact time;
the version of the terms and conditions and policy that the acceptance concerned;
the exact text of the checkbox label;
the context, e.g., seller registration or a specific order;
an evidence identifier allowing the event to be reconstructed.

This can be implemented in several correct ways: in the existing account event log, order history, audit log, or a separate acceptance register. The choice of tables and names is a technical decision. The condition is that the document is versioned and immutable, and the account or order record clearly indicates this version.
Minimal variant for Artovni:

Each published version of the terms and conditions has an identifier, an effective date, and immutable content - e.g., a versioned PDF file or a locked revision in the CMS. A file hash can serve as additional proof.
An existing account creation event records the terms and conditions version identifier and the acceptance time. There is no need to copy the entire terms and conditions to each record.
If the checkbox text is part of an immutable version of the form or application release, it can be reconstructed from that version; it does not need to be duplicated in every record.

For an order, the versions of documents relevant to that transaction or a checkout snapshot are recorded. Acceptance of account terms and conditions does not substitute proof of information and conditions for a specific sale.

There is no need to record the IP address or user-agent 'just in case.' They can be added after a risk analysis and legal basis assessment, but the primary evidence is the consistent linking of the user or order, time, and immutable content version.

The mere fact that a button was disabled without checking the checkbox is not sufficient proof if the platform cannot reconstruct the event and document version. If the current data model allows this to be done reliably and immutably, it may be sufficient without a new table.

blocks.text: When consent is needed and how to prove it

segments.text: Consent is typical for optional marketing, non-essential cookies, and certain additional features. It must be voluntary, specific, informed, unambiguous, not pre-checked, and as easy to withdraw as to give.

Proof of consent should be available in a single controlled evidentiary source, not solely in a mailing tool without its own export and history. This can be an existing event log or a separate register; the law does not dictate the name or structure of the table. The proof should include:
the person or account;
the controller and the purpose;
the channel: email, SMS, phone, push - separately if they differ in scope;
the exact text and version of the clause;
the time, source, and method of granting;
the status and time of withdrawal;
the systems to which consent was transferred.

blocks.label: STOP
blocks.text: Do not include in the terms and conditions that mandatory acceptance means consent to 'partner marketing,' profiling, and all channels. Such consent will not be voluntary or sufficiently specific.
Cookies and similar technologies

segments.text: Technologies necessary for transmission or a service requested by the user can operate without consent.
Analytics, advertising, personalization, and other optional technologies do not activate before consent.
The first layer provides equally easy 'accept' and 'reject' options; the user can select categories.
Withdrawal is constantly available and stops future operation.
The platform records the decision identifier, the version of the panel/list of providers, categories, time, and the change in decision.
A new provider or a new purpose requires updating the information and, if it goes beyond the granted scope, a new user decision.

blocks.text: Individual rights

segments.text: The platform has a single request channel and a process to identify which systems and roles the matter concerns. It generally responds within one month; for complex cases, it may extend the deadline by another two months, but it informs about this and the reasons within the first month.

Account deletion does not mean immediate erasure of all orders. The platform deletes or anonymizes data it no longer needs, and data subject to accounting, tax, DAC7, DSA, defense of claims, or incident response is blocked until the relevant deadline and not used for new purposes.

blocks.text: Data breaches

segments.text: The process involves detection, containment, risk assessment, evidence preservation, and decision on notification. If a breach is likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals, the controller notifies the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (UODO) without undue delay, where feasible within 72 hours of becoming aware of it. In case of high risk, it also informs the individuals, unless a statutory exception applies.

chapters.title: 13. DSA: reporting, moderation, and seller traceability

segments.text: The DSA applies to intermediary services in the EU. A marketplace is typically a hosting service and an online platform; some specific obligations depend on its size. However, an exemption does not mean that a micro-platform has no DSA obligations.

blocks.text: Minimum requirements to implement regardless of specific exemptions

segments.text: a contact point for authorities and for users, without mandating a specific automated tool;
terms of service describing content/offer restrictions, moderation tools, and operating procedures;
a mechanism for reporting illegal content/products with acknowledgment of receipt and a decision;
efficient removal or blocking upon obtaining actual knowledge, while preserving evidence;
clear justification for restricting, suspending, or terminating an offer/account when required by the DSA;
a procedure for reporting suspected criminal offenses that endanger life or safety to authorities;
publication of required information on moderation, unless a specific exemption applies.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: DSA and GPSR contact points can use the same contact page, inbox, and reporting table. However, the public page should clearly indicate the path for authorities and the path for users/consumers, be accessible without logging in, and lead to a human. For authorities, an email alias directed to the same queue can be published; for users, a form and email should remain. Maintaining two applications is not necessary.
Notice-and-action mechanism

segments.text: The form allows specifying the exact offer/content or its URL, explaining the illegality, attaching justification and evidence, providing name/company name and email, and making a declaration of acting in good faith and providing complete information. Contact details have an exception for specific reports concerning child sexual abuse material. The platform:
automatically confirms receipt;
assesses completeness and priority - product safety, fraud, and threats to life have a faster track;
decides in a timely, consistent, and objective manner;
informs the reporter of the decision and the possibility of appeal, if applicable;
informs the seller of the restriction with a specific justification, unless the law prohibits disclosure;
records evidence, basis, date, person/system, and further actions;
checks identical offers and attempts at re-publication.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: In the MVP, use the existing support form and the existing request record. Add the type 'Illegal offer/content (DSA)', a field or space for the exact URL/ID, the justification for illegality, and the required declaration. Acknowledgment of receipt can be a simple email with a UUID. The status history, decision, and sent messages can remain in the same table or log. A separate moderation module is not a legal requirement.

blocks.text: Marketplace obligations triggered upon exceeding micro/small status

segments.text: After losing the exemption - taking into account the statutory transition period - the platform implements at least:

public display of data required by Article 30 on the offer interface;
compliance by design: an interface enabling the seller to provide all consumer and product information and reasonable offer checks;
notification to buyers of an illegal product/service that the platform has become aware of, concerning purchases from the previous 6 months; if no contact is available - public announcement;
internal complaint system and additional platform obligations provided by DSA.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: Even if the bootstrap utilizes the exemption from Articles 30-32 DSA, it is advisable to collect company data, BDO, product roles, and self-certification from the outset. They are needed for other regulations and prevent costly migration upon growth.
Proof of moderation decision - not necessarily a separate register

segments.text: Each decision must allow reconstruction of: content/offer, scope of restriction, facts, signal source, regulatory/legal basis, use of automation, time, justification sent to the user, appeal, and outcome. This can be an existing request record with event history. A separate 'decision register' is only needed when the current model overwrites decisions, does not retain the sent justification, or does not allow for the preparation of required reports. If the decision is subject to transfer to the DSA transparency database, the process performs this without disclosing personal data.

chapters.title: 14. P2B: fair rules for business users

segments.text: The P2B Regulation governs the relationship between providers of online intermediation services and business users offering goods or services to consumers in the EU. It protects business users in their dealings with the platform operator. As of the date of this guide, it remains in force; planned EU simplifications should be monitored, but not treated as enacted law.

blocks.text: Seller terms and conditions must explain

segments.text: conditions for acceptance, restriction, suspension, and termination of cooperation;
main parameters of ranking, their relative importance, and the influence of payments;
differences in the treatment of the operator's own offers and those of other sellers;
what data the seller has access to during and after the contract, and whether the operator shares data with third parties;
rights to descriptions, images, trademarks, and other content of the seller;
additional services, fees, commissions, and payment terms;
complaint/appeal process and mediators, if the obligation applies;
consequences of contract termination and access to data export.

blocks.text: Change of terms and conditions

segments.text: Changes are communicated on a durable medium at least 15 days in advance. The deadline must be longer if the seller requires technical or business adaptation. Exceptions include urgent legal obligations or unforeseen security risks. Do not apply changes retroactively unless permitted by law.
The platform stores each version, sending date, recipients, effective date, and content of the communication.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: For the MVP, immutable versions of the terms and conditions, recording the effective date, and a copy of the email sent to the seller list are sufficient. It is not necessary to build a document versioning center if the existing dispatch system and file storage can demonstrate the content, recipients, and time.
Restriction, suspension, and termination

segments.text: Restriction or suspension requires a specific justification on a durable medium before or at the time of action, depending on the situation.
Complete termination of service generally requires justification at least 30 days in advance.
Exceptions allow immediate action, including for legal obligations, urgent risks, or repeated infringements, but the reason must still be documented and communicated to the extent permitted.
The seller must have a real opportunity to explain the situation and regain access after resolving the issue, provided the law and safety permit.

blocks.text: Complaints and mediators

segments.text: The obligation to provide an internal complaint-handling system and identify at least two mediators does not apply to small enterprises as defined by the P2B Regulation. Medium-sized operators should have these elements. A small operator may implement them earlier as good practice but should not mistakenly claim an exemption solely because the marketplace is small - the enterprise's status is what matters.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: For a small operator, explanations to the seller can be handled via a standard ticket and email, provided the decision and response are retained. A dedicated complaints/mediation portal is an obligation or need for a later stage, not an automatic requirement for a bootstrap.

chapters.title: 15. DAC7: seller data and annual reporting

segments.text: DAC7 is not a tax imposed by the platform. It is an obligation of due diligence, collection, verification, and reporting by the platform operator, if the software enables sellers to perform the reported activities and the operator knows or can reasonably determine the transaction value.

Software used solely for payment processing, listing or advertising, or redirecting users to another service may fall outside the definition if it does not perform an additional platform function. A typical marketplace that processes orders and charges commission usually requires an assessment of whether the operator is a Reporting Platform Operator.

blocks.text: Which sellers of goods are excluded from the report

segments.text: For the sale of goods, a seller is excluded as an "excluded seller" only if they meet both conditions for the entire reporting period:
fewer than 30 transactions; and
the total consideration paid or credited does not exceed EUR 2,000.
Exactly 30 transactions or exceeding EUR 2,000 means this exclusion does not apply. For personal services and other reported categories, this goods threshold does not apply in the same way.

blocks.label: IMPORTANT
blocks.text: The platform should still collect data to assess the status. One cannot wait until the end of the year to discover that a seller exceeded the threshold but did not provide their TIN or residency.
What to collect and determine

segments.text: Depending on the individual/entity and applicable regulations: full name or company name, principal address, country of residence, TIN and issuing country, VAT number, date of birth, company registration number, and required business information. The financial account identifier and its holder's details are included to the extent required by law only if available to the operator. It is not necessary to collect the full IBAN solely to make it available.

For the report, the system aggregates quarterly at least the number of transactions, the total consideration, as defined by DAC7, and any collected or withheld commissions, fees, and taxes. Refunded and cancelled amounts must be handled according to an approved method, not manually removed from the report without a trace.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: DAC7 does not immediately require a dedicated module. With a small number of sellers, the platform can prepare a controlled export from the order database and Stripe, combine it with seller data, and validate it in a spreadsheet according to documented instructions. Conditions: a consistent method, change control, the ability to reproduce the result, and timely submission of the report. Automate when manual reconciliation becomes prone to omissions.

chapters.title: 16. E-commerce accessibility from June 28, 2025

segments.text: The Polish Accessibility Act covers e-commerce services. A micro-entrepreneur providing the service is exempt, but a small or medium operator is not. Micro means fewer than 10 people and an annual turnover or balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 2 million, taking into account rules for affiliated enterprises.

blocks.label: DECISION
blocks.text: Even if the operator is a micro-entrepreneur, they should build accessibility from the beginning. The exemption may disappear with growth, and rebuilding the catalog, checkout, and seller panel after years is significantly more expensive.
What needs to be accessible

segments.text: registration and login, including authentication;
search engine, filters, ranking, and product card;
information about the seller, price, warnings, and delivery;
shopping cart, checkout, payment selection, and confirmation;
withdrawal form, complaint form, product reporting, and contact;
account panel and order history;
documents, messages, and customer service related to the service.

blocks.text: Practical acceptance criteria

segments.text: full keyboard operation without focus traps;
visible focus and logical navigation order;
correct headings, field labels, and error messages read by a screen reader;
alternative text for meaningful images; product images cannot be the sole carrier of important warnings;
adequate contrast, magnification, and reflow without loss of functionality;
information is not conveyed solely by color, position, or sound;
forms allow error correction, and data confirmation before payment;
accessible CAPTCHA, MFA, time limits, and chat;
understandable language and accessible downloadable files.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: An in-house auditing platform is not needed to start. The critical path can be checked manually with a keyboard, magnification, and a popular screen reader, errors found can be recorded in a standard task system, and testing can be repeated after corrections. Automated tools are helpful but do not replace manual traversal of registration–product–cart–payment–contact.
Information on accessibility and non-compliance

segments.text: The operator covered by the Act publishes in the terms and conditions or an equivalent document information on how the service meets accessibility requirements and keeps it up to date. If the service ceases to meet the requirements, it takes corrective actions and fulfills the obligation to notify the competent authority in accordance with the Act. Invoking disproportionate burden or fundamental change requires a documented assessment – it is not a general budget exemption.

chapters.title: 17. Cybersecurity and KSC/NIS2

segments.text: Security is not an add-on to GDPR. The marketplace stores seller identification data, customer addresses, purchase history, and compliance documents. Full payout statements may remain with Stripe/PSP, but account takeover in the marketplace can still allow changes to the offer, price, contact details, or payment account linkage.

blocks.text: Minimum for every operator

segments.text: MFA for administration and for local high-risk operations. If account changes and payouts are handled exclusively by Stripe in its hosted process, MFA/step-up for this activity is provided by Stripe - Artovnia does not duplicate the screen or the account;
principle of least privilege and separation of customer service, finance, compliance, and administration;
transmission encryption, secure storage of secrets, and encryption of sensitive repositories;
log of changes to seller data, prices, products, permissions, and payouts;

if the platform itself allows changing the account or PSP account - confirmation outside the current session; if the Artovnia panel only shows history and statistics, secure authentication of the panel is sufficient, along with verification that local actions cannot change payout details;
security patches, vulnerability scanning, and testing before major changes;
backups separated from the production environment and regular restore testing;
abuse monitoring: account takeovers, unusual payouts, mass offer changes, return of blocked products;
vulnerability reporting and incident handling process;
business continuity plan and contact list for PSP, hosting, UODO, CSIRT, UOKiK, and product authorities.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: A “change log” can be an existing application log or event history, and “monitoring” can initially mean provider alerts and a daily review of key events by a designated person. Do not create your own security center. First, secure administration, backups, secrets, updates, and the response procedure.

blocks.label: DECISION
blocks.text: In the Artovnia/Etsy model, where the seller chooses the courier, packs, and ships themselves, the operator does not manage the physical supply chain. They should only require truthful information about costs and deadlines, a tracking number when used, and a process for loss, withdrawal, and claims. Full management of couriers, warehouses, and transport conditions arises only when the operator offers its own delivery or fulfillment.
When an average marketplace falls under KSC

segments.text: The amendment to the KSC implementing NIS2 is effective from April 3, 2026. A provider of an online trading platform is located in the digital sector. An entity meeting size and sectoral criteria may be a significant entity. In simplified terms, a typical small and medium-sized enterprise – fewer than 250 people and revenue up to EUR 50 million or a balance sheet total up to EUR 43 million, but not meeting the criteria for a small enterprise – should conduct a formal self-identification. Affiliated entities and statutory exceptions are also considered.

blocks.label: DEADLINE
blocks.text: An entity meeting the criteria on the date the amendment enters into force shall submit an application to the KSC Register by October 3, 2026, and implement the obligations and use of S46 by April 3, 2027. A new or growing entity checks deadlines calculated from the later fulfillment of the prerequisites.
What to implement after qualification

segments.text: risk-based information security management system;
approved management responsibility and training;
incident, continuity, crisis, backup, and recovery management;

digital supply chain security: hosting, cloud, Stripe/PSP, email, helpdesk, analytics, software vendors, and administrators. This does not concern seller couriers unless the operator itself provides or organizes logistics as its own service;
secure acquisition, development, and maintenance of systems, and vulnerability handling;
cryptography, access, asset, personnel, and MFA policies;
performance indicators and periodic reviews;
registration, communication, and reporting through appropriate KSC/S46 channels.

A serious incident requires early warning no later than 24 hours after detection and reporting no later than 72 hours; further information and the final report are provided in accordance with the Act and instructions from the relevant CSIRT. The internal process should escalate immediately, not at the 23rd hour.

blocks.label: IMPORTANT
blocks.text: The fact that KSC obligations are deferred until 2027 does not defer GDPR, payment security, or the obligation to reasonably secure the platform. The transition year is for implementation, not for waiting.

product recall drill: can you find sellers, batches, and buyers within hours.

blocks.label: EVIDENCE
blocks.text: The operator should be able to compile not only sales figures but also: compliance gaps, response times, overdue refunds, unanswered complaints, products without the required responsible person, sellers with DAC7/BDO deficiencies in their scope, and the result of the recall test. In MVP, saved queries and a controlled spreadsheet/periodic report are sufficient; a dashboard is convenient for scaling.

chapters.title: 20. Four business models - specific decisions

blocks.text: A. Bootstrap with handicrafts, like Artovnia

segments.text: Recommended start: only entrepreneurs from Poland/EU, no shipping from outside the EU, no operator fulfillment, no high-risk categories. The seller is the party to the sale, PSP handles payment separation.
What to build first:
onboarding of the manufacturer-artisan and their BDO/packaging;
simple but mandatory GPSR documentation and batch identification;
separate gateways for food-contact ceramics, candles, cosmetics, and children's products;
manufacturer and warning cards;
checkout, withdrawal, complaint, and a fast security channel;
proof of terms and conditions and separate marketing consents;
export of orders, commissions, and DAC7 data.
Do not allow at the start: cosmetics 'without papers', toys without CE marking, mugs without food-contact proof, dropshipping imports, and claims that 'handicrafts are not subject to GPSR/BDO'.

blocks.text: B. Sports store adding a marketplace

segments.text: The most important thing is to separate the two roles. For own goods, the operator is the seller; for partner offers, an intermediary. The customer must see this on the listing, product page, in the cart, on the confirmation, and in the complaint process.
What to build:
a "sold by: store" or "sold by: partner" marker in every relevant place;
separate sales documents and VAT/commission settlement;
routing of complaints and withdrawals according to the seller;
category gates for helmets/PPE, electronics, supplements, and children's products;
control over favoring own offers in ranking and P2B description;
a shared checkout, but separate orders, refunds, and payouts;
own BDO obligations for goods/operator, independent of partners.

blocks.label: STOP
blocks.text: The store's brand in the header cannot lead the customer to reasonably assume the store is the seller of all products when the agreement attempts to transfer responsibility to an invisible partner.
C. Medium-sized general product marketplace

segments.text: Do not launch 'everything' with a single control. The platform creates a category program with owners and risk levels. It automates DSA/DAC7 onboarding, document repository, BDO, moderation, pricing, recalls, and notifications.

Once the threshold is exceeded, readiness for full DSA platform obligations is required. As a medium-sized online platform operator, one must formally check KSC and the registration deadline. PAD applies unless a micro-enterprise exemption is in place. P2B requires a complaint/mediation system within the scope defined by the regulation.

blocks.text: D. Marketplace 1000 florists, each with its own storefront

segments.text: Each florist is a separate seller. The storefront displays their data, delivery terms, and local reach, but the operator maintains consistent minimum rules.
Key functions:
onboarding and re-verification of 1000 entities without manual data re-entry;
local order routing to the correct florist and a clear contract page;
cut-off times, availability, and substitution of flowers confirmed before purchase, not after;
proof of photo/description of the arrangement and the scope of permissible changes;
information on price, delivery, freshness, and withdrawal – an exception for perishable goods applied only to products actually meeting the criteria;
quality complaints and prompt proof of condition upon delivery;
BDO/packaging assigned to the florist responsible for packing, or a fulfillment model described in the contract;
category of additional gifts separately: alcohol, food, cosmetics, candles, and toys cannot pass the 'flowers' gateway.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: For 1000 storefronts, centralize rules, evidence, and deadlines, but do not mix responsibilities. One platform does not mean one seller, one BDO number, or one sales document.

chapters.title: 21. Document and Procedure Package to Prepare

blocks.text: Documents visible to customers

segments.text: Platform and sales terms and conditions, with a clear division between operator and seller.
Seller information and terms specific to their offer.
Privacy policy.
Cookie policy/preference panel.
Information on ranking, advertising, personalization, and reviews.
Withdrawal instructions and a sample form.
Complaint process.
Channel for reporting illegal content/products and security issues.
Information on service availability.

blocks.text: Documents and procedures for sellers

segments.text: Seller terms and conditions/agreement compliant with P2B.
Product data and document standards.
Policy on prohibited and restricted products.
Category instructions and admission criteria.
Declaration of roles: manufacturer/importer/distributor, fulfillment, and responsible person in the EU.
BDO/EPR declaration and evidence.
DAC7 questionnaire and obligations.
Rules for pricing, promotions, ranking, advertising, and reviews.
SLA for fulfillment, withdrawals, complaints, and security.
Procedure for suspension, appeal, termination, and data export.

blocks.text: Operator's internal documents

segments.text: Responsibility model document.
RODO processing activity register, role map, retention policy, and processor list.
Data breach and rights violation procedure.
DSA procedure and the ability to reconstruct moderation decisions in existing reports/logs.
GPSR procedure, product recall, and traceability exercises.
Category gateway matrix.
Seller verification and exception procedure.
DAC7 procedure and reporting calendar.
BDO/operator-seller-fulfillment procedure.
30-day price, review, and ranking procedure.
Security, incident, business continuity, and backup plan.
Availability assessment, testing, and remediation plan.
DSA/PAD/P2B/KSC self-identification updated annually.
Legal changes register and owner for each area.

blocks.label: EVIDENCE
blocks.text: A document without an owner, version, review date, and functioning process is marketing material, not a compliance control.

blocks.label: PRACTICE
blocks.text: The 'document package' does not mean 14 separate applications or even 14 files. A small operator can maintain a single operational manual with chapters, checklists, and templates, storing evidence in the systems where it is generated. Separate them only when different permissions, owners, or update cycles require it.

chapters.title: 23. Most Common Misconceptions

rows: Myth
Correct Rule
"We will write in the terms and conditions that the seller is responsible for everything."
The agreement divides responsibility between parties but does not exclude the operator's statutory obligations.
"The law requires a separate acceptance table."

The law requires proof of provision and the ability to reproduce the applicable version, not a specific table. A consistent link between an account/order event and an immutable document version is sufficient.
"A locked button and checkbox are always sufficient as proof."
There must be a persistent event that allows identification of the person or context, time, and version. This can be stored in an existing log, not necessarily in a separate table.
"Accepting the terms and conditions constitutes GDPR consent."
This is a contractual statement. Order fulfillment is usually not based on consent.
"Handmade items are not subject to GPSR."
A craftsperson operating commercially is a producer; scale does not remove the safety obligation. Occasional private sales are a separate case.
"Every product requires a form with weight, dimensions, and a hundred fields."

The common minimum is short, and industry-specific fields are activated only for the relevant category. A clear photo of the label can convey some information, but key data and warnings must be visible and accessible.
"Below 1 ton, there is no BDO."
A threshold may grant exemption from certain obligations upon meeting conditions, but it does not automatically remove the registration and reporting requirement.
"Every seller must have a BDO."
No. First, a distinction is made between private sales/unregistered activity and entrepreneurs, and only then between packaging role, import, and product group.
"Dropshipping means the wholesaler is responsible."
Dropshipping is a logistics method. The seller and the platform still need to determine the importer, the EU-based representative, VAT/customs, returns, and BDO.
"Since Stripe has an account, the platform must copy the IBAN."

No. For DAC7, the account identifier is reported when available to the operator; for an exempted micro/small marketplace under Article 30 of the DSA, it generally does not apply. Once Article 30 is applicable, the integration with the PSP must already allow the obligation to be fulfilled.
"A GPSR contact point means a separate form for authorities."
No. It can be a public email/alias or a shared form with a clear category and appropriate routing. Authorities and consumers can be directed to the same backend.
"A UUID from a regular request is not a case number."
It is a sufficient operational identifier if it is persistent, unique, and searchable. GPSR does not mandate a specific format for the number.
"We are small, so DSA does not apply to us."
The exemption for micro/small platforms covers only certain obligations, not the entirety of the DSA.
"Account deletion means deletion of all orders."
Data required for legal, tax, DAC7, dispute resolution, and safety purposes will be retained with restricted use until the relevant deadline.
"One product card can serve every seller."
Only if the product, manufacturer, variant, responsible entity, and warnings are indeed identical.
"Compliance is a launch project."
It is an ongoing operation: deadlines, re-verifications, audits, incidents, reports, and legal changes.

blocks.text: How to Update Without Chaos

segments.text: Record changes in law or new interpretations by authorities.
Indicate which roles, categories, screens, terms, and evidence are affected.
Decide on the deadline and transition period.
Modify functionalities, operational instructions, and documents as a single package.
Test with user scenarios and offers.
Notify sellers of the change in advance, as required by P2B, unless a legal exception applies.
Retain the old version and proof of entry into force.
